documents.title: Academic Integrity (AI guideline)
documents.stance_why: The guideline says "Whether you determine AI use is appropriate in your course or not", so the decision rests with each instructor, and the page only requires clear communication and use of the Academic Honor Policy; it sets no university-wide permission or ban.
documents.summary: Official AIEAC academic integrity guideline for faculty: instructors set and communicate AI rules in syllabi, treat misuse via the Honor Policy, avoid AI detectors, and follow an early-intervention process with students.

units.why: The guideline sentence tells instructors to set expectations and define acceptable AI use "in your course syllabus and materials", so it is a communication rule for instructors (course-start, should); P09 fits because it requires AI expectations in the syllabus.
units.anchor: setting expectations and clearly defining acceptable AI use in your course syllabus and materials

units.why: "Whether you determine AI use is appropriate in your course or not" leaves the allow/ban decision to each instructor, so it is a delegation rule (P04), not a default stance.
units.anchor: Whether you determine AI use is appropriate in your course or not
units.policy: Each instructor determines whether AI use is appropriate in their course.

units.why: The same sentence says "clearly communicating your AI policies with students in your course syllabus and assignment instructions" is expected of instructors regardless of the decision; this is a distinct communication rule coded as P09 (the delegation part is the previous unit).
units.anchor: clearly communicating your AI policies with students in your course syllabus and assignment instructions

units.why: "follow the FSU Academic Honor Policy process when alleged academic misconduct occurs" binds instructors to the formal integrity process for suspected AI misuse (when-misuse, must); P36 is the integrity-process type.
units.anchor: Be sure to follow the FSU Academic Honor Policy process when alleged academic misconduct occurs.

units.why: The passage states that the Honor Policy "addresses AI-related misconduct such as cheating, plagiarism, and falsification", i.e. AI misuse is handled as academic misconduct (informs, P36).
units.anchor: addresses AI-related misconduct such as cheating, plagiarism, and falsification

units.why: "honors students' rights and due process" says AI-misconduct cases protect student fairness and process; P64 (fairness in AI integrity cases) fits better than the generic P36 since the point is due process.
units.anchor: honors students’ rights and due process

units.why: Defines cheating via the example of unauthorized AI during an exam; it classifies exam AI misuse as misconduct (P36). P22 would fit only if it banned exam AI outright; here it defines the misconduct.
units.anchor: Use of unauthorized AI tools during an exam is an example of cheating with AI.

units.why: "Presenting AI-generated content as though it is original work is an example of plagiarism" classifies undisclosed AI-produced submissions as plagiarism (P36); P19 states a ban on submission, whereas this defines the misconduct category.
units.anchor: Presenting AI-generated content as though it is original work is an example of plagiarism.

units.why: "use of AI to generate false citations, documents, or signatures" is named as falsification, a form of misconduct, so it is classified under P36.
units.anchor: Examples of falsification include use of AI to generate false citations, documents, or signatures.

units.why: "The ability to hold students accountable ... depends on how clearly you communicate your expectations" gives the reason instructors must state AI expectations; P09 is the closest type since it concerns stating expectations.
units.anchor: The ability to hold students accountable for their use of AI in coursework depends on
units.policy: The ability to hold students accountable for their use of AI in coursework depends on how clearly you communicate your expectations.

units.why: Cites a "2025 survey" by the AI advisory committee finding student anxiety when AI instructions are unclear; this is evidence about AI and students, so P55.
units.anchor: students reported high levels of anxiety when instructions for AI use in an assignment were
units.policy: students reported high levels of anxiety when instructions for AI use in an assignment were not clearly communicated

units.why: "Open conversations with students about the acceptable use of AI" is advice to instructors to discuss AI rules, a communication practice (P09 closest).
units.anchor: Open conversations with students about the acceptable use of AI

units.why: The same sentence gives a rationale: such conversations prepare students "to apply AI responsibly in future careers and professional environments", a career-preparation rationale (P44).
units.anchor: preparing them to apply AI responsibly in future careers and professional environments

units.why: "The traffic light framework provides a helpful structure for communicating AI policies" recommends named tiers (traffic light) for syllabi, which is P05.
units.anchor: The traffic light framework provides a helpful structure for communicating AI policies to students.

units.why: The heading "Don't Use AI Detection Tools" and the sentence that detectors "are not licensed by the university and are highly unreliable" tell instructors not to rely on detectors as evidence, so P39.
units.anchor: these tools are not licensed by the university and are highly unreliable
units.policy: AI detectors are not licensed by the university and are highly unreliable; instructors are told not to use AI detection tools.

units.why: Explains detector unreliability: "AI detectors often generate false positives and are subject to hallucination", supporting P39 as a factual claim.
units.anchor: AI detectors often generate false positives and are subject to hallucination

units.why: Warns that content shared with detectors "may be retained by the vendor and used to train its large language model", causing unauthorized disclosure of protected information; a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: content shared with them may be retained by the vendor and used to train its
units.policy: content shared with them may be retained by the vendor and used to train its large language model

units.why: Says the university provides instructors "tools to help ensure academic integrity, including a licensed plagiarism detection tool"; this is a similarity-check tool offered for integrity work (P40).
units.anchor: The university provides all instructors tools to help ensure academic integrity

units.why: "early intervention is key" followed by instructions to email the FDA office and then contact the student tells instructors how to start the integrity process; coded P36.
units.anchor: When it comes to addressing alleged academic misconduct, early intervention is key.

units.why: "to determine if the student has had a previous violation" gives the required first step on suspicion of misconduct, part of the integrity process (P36).
units.anchor: to determine if the student has had a previous violation

units.why: "review the AI use expectations you included in your syllabus ... Were any expectations omitted, unclear, or open to interpretation?" asks instructors to check their own communication before escalating, which is P57 (gather context before escalating).
units.anchor: Before talking with your student, review the AI use expectations you included in your syllabus,
units.policy: Before talking with your student, review the AI use expectations you included in your syllabus, assignment instructions, and Canvas course site.

units.why: "Gather any documentation and create a brief timeline" tells instructors to assemble process evidence of suspected misuse; P40 (evidence used to identify misuse).
units.anchor: Gather any documentation and create a brief timeline of the suspected misconduct.

units.why: Because AI "can produce hallucinations and incorrect or broken links", instructors should cross-reference student citations; this is a verification step for evidence (P40).
units.anchor: cross-reference links and other information (eg, citations) the student provides

units.why: "Do not record meetings" is a procedural rule for the conversation with the student about suspected misconduct, under P57 (talking with the student).
units.anchor: Do not record meetings

units.why: "use open-ended questions to explore and address the allegations" after acknowledging circumstances tells instructors to hear the student out before escalation (P57).
units.anchor: use open-ended questions to explore and address the allegations

units.why: "Ask for evidence of effort and learning outside of class, pointing out gaps in the student's explanations" checks understanding by having the student explain their work (P34).
units.anchor: Ask for evidence of effort and learning outside of class, pointing out gaps in the
units.policy: Ask for evidence of effort and learning outside of class, pointing out gaps in the student’s explanations.

units.why: "send them to your student within 48 hours" requires written notes of the discussion to the student, a transparency and fairness step in a misconduct case (P64).
units.anchor: write detailed notes summarizing the discussion and send them to your student within 48 hours

units.why: "prioritize proposed sanctions that educate and remediate, not merely penalize" is guidance on sanctions in AI-misconduct cases; it fits P36 (handled via integrity process) because it names no concrete penalties (so not P37).
units.anchor: It is always a best practice to prioritize proposed sanctions that educate and remediate, not
units.policy: It is always a best practice to prioritize proposed sanctions that educate and remediate, not merely penalize.

units.why: "be prepared to compile documentation ... and forward it to FDA" is a step in the Academic Honor Policy process when a discussion supports allegations (P36).
units.anchor: compile documentation (eg, your syllabus, all evidence, notes, timeline of event, completed Academic Honor Policy
units.policy: compile documentation (eg, your syllabus, all evidence, notes, timeline of event, completed Academic Honor Policy resolution form)

documents.title: Resources for Faculty (AIEAC guidelines)
documents.stance_why: The page directs faculty to "Determine when AI tools may or may not be used in your courses"; the university policies are still being developed ("developing policies for consideration by the Faculty Senate"), so no stance is set centrally.
documents.summary: Faculty hub listing five AIEAC guidelines (literacy, privacy, integrity, access, teaching), the interim policy status, university-provided tools and training.

units.why: The intro says FSU "continues to develop and refine resources to support the responsible use of AI in teaching and learning", a statement of institutional purpose (P56) and of ongoing refinement.
units.anchor: FSU continues to develop and refine resources to support the responsible use of AI

units.why: Describes the AIEAC as established for "assessing AI's effect on learning and student engagement"; it commits to gathering evidence on learning effects (P55).
units.anchor: assessing AI's effect on learning and student engagement

units.why: "Develop a foundational knowledge of AI technology's capabilities, limitations, and consequences before using it" tells faculty to learn AI before adopting it, i.e. P63 (support faculty in learning AI).
units.anchor: Develop a foundational knowledge of AI technology’s capabilities, limitations, and consequences before using it in
units.policy: Develop a foundational knowledge of AI technology’s capabilities, limitations, and consequences before using it in various academic and professional contexts.

units.why: "Ethical use should be a primary consideration when making decisions about implementing AI" sets a principle for faculty decisions; P56 (framework principles) fits since it names no concrete harm (so not P53).
units.anchor: Ethical use should be a primary consideration when making decisions about implementing AI.

units.why: "Ensure your use of AI complies with data privacy laws and institutional policies" binds faculty to privacy compliance (P50).
units.anchor: Ensure your use of AI complies with data privacy laws and institutional policies, safeguarding personal,
units.policy: Ensure your use of AI complies with data privacy laws and institutional policies, safeguarding personal, academic, and research data.

units.why: The Academic Integrity guideline summary asks faculty to set expectations and define acceptable AI use "in your course syllabus and materials" (P09).
units.anchor: setting expectations and clearly defining acceptable AI use in your course syllabus and materials

units.why: Faculty "be sure to follow the FSU Academic Honor Policy process when alleged academic misconduct occurs" (P36).
units.anchor: Be sure to follow the FSU Academic Honor Policy process when alleged academic misconduct occurs.

units.why: "Consider disparities in resources such as cost and accessibility when selecting AI tools for courses" is an equity rule for course tool choice (P51).
units.anchor: Consider disparities in resources such as cost and accessibility when selecting AI tools for courses.

units.why: "you may use AI tools not directly licensed by the university ... make sure they are approved through appropriate university channels" limits tool choice to approved ones (P50, vetted tools).
units.anchor: While you may use AI tools not directly licensed by the university, make sure they
units.policy: While you may use AI tools not directly licensed by the university, make sure they are approved through appropriate university channels.

units.why: "Determine when AI tools may or may not be used in your courses and clearly communicate your decision" leaves the allow/ban decision to the instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Determine when AI tools may or may not be used in your courses and clearly
units.policy: Determine when AI tools may or may not be used in your courses and clearly communicate your decision to students.

units.why: "AI tools should be used in ways that support student learning outcomes and promote transparency and accountability" is a general principle for AI use in courses (P56).
units.anchor: AI tools should be used in ways that support student learning outcomes and promote transparency
units.policy: AI tools should be used in ways that support student learning outcomes and promote transparency and accountability between instructors and students.

units.why: Says policies are being developed "for consideration by the Faculty Senate and Office of the Provost", showing the university policy is not final (P54).
units.anchor: developing policies for consideration by the Faculty Senate and Office of the Provost

units.why: "be sure you know your responsibilities when it comes to protecting the security and privacy of your personal data and intellectual property" is an interim privacy duty (P50).
units.anchor: In the meantime, be sure you know your responsibilities when it comes to protecting the
units.policy: In the meantime, be sure you know your responsibilities when it comes to protecting the security and privacy of your personal data and intellectual property.

units.why: "only AI tools approved through appropriate university channels are recommended for use by FSU faculty, students, and staff" recommends vetted tools for data protection (P50).
units.anchor: only AI tools approved through appropriate university channels are recommended for use

units.why: "The university provides several AI tools and technologies to support teaching and learning" announces sanctioned tools under vendor agreements (P17).
units.anchor: The university provides several AI tools and technologies to support teaching and learning at FSU.

units.why: The Faculty Innovators coffee chats offer faculty events on AI in teaching and research, matching P63 (support faculty in learning AI).
units.anchor: Join a Coffee Chat at the Innovation Hub to learn more about AI in teaching
units.policy: Join a Coffee Chat at the Innovation Hub to learn more about AI in teaching and research.

units.why: Training offered "at no cost to FSU students, faculty, and staff" (Google AI certificate) addresses access and cost (P51).
units.anchor: The course is available at no cost to FSU students, faculty, and staff.

documents.title: Resources for Students (incl. Traffic Light framework)
documents.stance_why: "Your professor determines if and how AI technologies may be used in coursework", and a Green/Yellow/Red traffic-light template is offered; this is tiers plus delegation.
documents.summary: Student hub: instructors decide AI use, students must follow course rules, ask when unsure, protect data, use approved tools; a three-tier traffic-light syllabus template is given.

units.why: The intro says FSU is "committed to providing students with AI technologies that enhance the student experience and promote deeper learning", an institution-level purpose statement (P56) with an encouraging stance.
units.anchor: committed to providing students with artificial intelligence (AI) technologies that enhance the student experience

units.why: "preparing tomorrow's leaders with the skills they need to apply AI technologies across disciplines" is a career-readiness rationale (P44).
units.anchor: preparing tomorrow's leaders with the skills they need to apply AI technologies across disciplines

units.why: "Your professor determines if and how AI technologies may be used in coursework" delegates the decision to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: Your professor determines if and how AI technologies may be used in coursework.

units.why: "Be sure to read the course syllabus carefully for guidance on the use of AI technologies" tells students to check the syllabus for rules; P10 is the nearest type (student checks before using AI).
units.anchor: read the course syllabus carefully for guidance on the use of AI technologies

units.why: "if you need clarification, reach out to your professor before you use AI in your class assignments" is an ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: reach out to your professor before you use AI in your class assignments

units.why: "Build the knowledge and skills needed to work with AI tools effectively and responsibly" frames AI skill as something students should develop (P44).
units.anchor: Build the knowledge and skills needed to work with AI tools effectively and responsibly.

units.why: "Validate AI-generated content carefully" requires checking AI output (P31).
units.anchor: Validate AI-generated content carefully

units.why: "use AI to support your learning rather than replace your thinking" keeps the student as the thinker (P32).
units.anchor: use AI to support your learning rather than replace your thinking

units.why: "Protect your own personal information and the privacy and data of other students and the university when using AI tools" is a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: Protect your own personal information and the privacy and data of other students and the
units.policy: Protect your own personal information and the privacy and data of other students and the university when using AI tools.

units.why: "Do not share login credentials, course materials, research, or other information with AI tools that are not approved by the university" bars uploading course materials to unapproved AI; P49 chosen over P50 since course materials are named.
units.anchor: Do not share login credentials, course materials, research, or other information with AI tools that
units.policy: Do not share login credentials, course materials, research, or other information with AI tools that are not approved by the university.

units.why: "Follow guidelines established for AI use in each course and assignment" ties student conduct to per-course or per-assignment rules set by the instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Follow guidelines established for AI use in each course and assignment.

units.why: "If these guidelines are unclear, ask your instructor before using AI" is an explicit ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: If these guidelines are unclear, ask your instructor before using AI.

units.why: "Work submitted should reflect your own learning" requires submitted work to be the student's own (P29).
units.anchor: Work submitted should reflect your own learning

units.why: "Use AI tools authorized by the university" because others "may collect your data, charge unexpected fees, or reuse content" is a vetted-tools and privacy rule (P50).
units.anchor: Use AI tools authorized by the university as other tools may collect your data, charge
units.policy: Use AI tools authorized by the university as other tools may collect your data, charge unexpected fees, or reuse content that you submit.

units.why: "Approved tools have been reviewed, vetted, and include agreements that protect users and university information" explains why approved tools are preferred (P50).
units.anchor: Approved tools have been reviewed, vetted, and include agreements that protect users and university information.

units.why: "While AI can help generate ideas, explain concepts, or support studying" lists acceptable support uses; P12 chosen as the primary since explaining concepts is the central tutor use, though brainstorming (P15) and study aids (P14) are also named.
units.anchor: While AI can help generate ideas, explain concepts, or support studying

units.why: "it should not replace your own learning or original research" bars AI from substituting for student thinking (P32).
units.anchor: it should not replace your own learning or original research

units.why: "Recognize that human inquiry, critical analysis, and engagement are essential to your academic development" gives a skill-building rationale (P41).
units.anchor: Recognize that human inquiry, critical analysis, and engagement are essential to your academic development.

units.why: Policies are still "developing ... for consideration by the Faculty Senate and Office of the Provost", showing provisional status (P54).
units.anchor: developing policies for consideration by the Faculty Senate and Office of the Provost

units.why: "only AI tools approved through appropriate university channels are recommended" recommends vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: only AI tools approved through appropriate university channels are recommended for use

units.why: "The university provides several AI tools and technologies to support teaching and learning" announces sanctioned tools (P17).
units.anchor: The university provides several AI tools and technologies to support teaching and learning at FSU.

units.why: "recommends clear language in course syllabi when the use of AI is either appropriate or prohibited" asks instructors to state AI expectations in syllabi (P09).
units.anchor: recommends clear language in course syllabi when the use of AI is either appropriate or
units.policy: recommends clear language in course syllabi when the use of AI is either appropriate or prohibited

units.why: "Your professor may utilize the Traffic Light Framework" introduces named Green/Yellow/Red tiers for AI use (P05).
units.anchor: Your professor may utilize the Traffic Light Framework* below for communicating when and how you
units.policy: Your professor may utilize the Traffic Light Framework* below for communicating when and how you may use AI in academic work.

units.why: Green Light: "Students are encouraged to use AI tools, such as Google Gemini or Microsoft Copilot" is a default-encourage statement (P02).
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to use AI tools, such as Google Gemini or Microsoft Copilot, to
units.policy: Students are encouraged to use AI tools, such as Google Gemini or Microsoft Copilot, to explore ideas and collaborate with others.

units.why: Green Light: "All AI-generated content must be cited" requires citation of AI output (P24).
units.anchor: All AI-generated content must be cited

units.why: Green Light: "its accuracy should be carefully evaluated" requires verifying AI output (P31).
units.anchor: its accuracy should be carefully evaluated

units.why: Green Light: "The course will include discussions on best practices for AI usage" means the course teaches AI use (P44).
units.anchor: The course will include discussions on best practices for AI usage.

units.why: Yellow Light: "AI-generated content may be incorporated, but it must be clearly cited and validated" allows AI output in specific assignments under conditions (P16).
units.anchor: For specific assignments, AI-generated content may be incorporated, but it must be clearly cited and
units.policy: For specific assignments, AI-generated content may be incorporated, but it must be clearly cited and validated.

units.why: Yellow Light: "AI tools may be used with caution" sets a conditional-permit tier default; coded as P02 (permit by default under caution).
units.anchor: AI tools may be used with caution.

units.why: Yellow Light: "Students are advised to consult with the instructor if unsure" is an ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: Students are advised to consult with the instructor if unsure about the appropriateness of AI
units.policy: Students are advised to consult with the instructor if unsure about the appropriateness of AI for a particular task.

units.why: Red Light: "AI tools are not permitted in this course" is a ban on AI for the course (P01).
units.anchor: AI tools are not permitted in this course.

units.why: Red Light: "All work must be completed independently, without the assistance of AI tools" requires student-only work (P19 used since it speaks to submitted work; the course-wide ban is the previous unit).
units.anchor: All work must be completed independently, without the assistance of AI tools.

units.why: Red Light: "Violations of this policy will result in academic penalties" states consequences without specifics; P37 is the closest, though no concrete penalty is given.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will result in academic penalties.

units.why: Describes "university-supported platforms" including Artes AI, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Zoom AI Companion, pointing to sanctioned tools (P17).
units.anchor: Compare university-supported platforms ranging from general chat assistants to specialized agentic tools

units.why: "available at no cost to FSU students, faculty, and staff" (Google AI certificate) is an access-cost statement (P51).
units.anchor: The course is available at no cost to FSU students, faculty, and staff.

notes: Only university-layer AIEAC web pages were included; no school, computing or course documents. FSU formal policy is still pending Faculty Senate/Provost. Faculty and student pages repeat some sentences from the integrity page; each page was coded on its own.
